newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanians pitch tents to protest at homes law.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanians pitch tents to protest at homes law.

text.p: Lithuanians pitched a sea of yellow, green and grey tents outside their parliament on Thursday, protesting that a plan to return homes to their pre-Soviet owners may leave them on the streets.

"Today is only a warning. If they pass a law in favour of the former owners, the whole front lawn of parliament will be covered by tents and people will stay here until the politicians capitulate," said an organiser.

About 150 people set up 25 tents on a lawn behind the house, jeering at politicians and vowing to brave the cool Lithuanian spring and stay until the law, which went through its first reading on Thursday, is scuppered.

"We defended the parliament in 1991, and now it wants to throw us into the street," said one protester, referring to a bloody Soviet crackdown in January 1991 which left 13 people dead during the Baltic state's drive for independence.
The government says no one will be thrown out of their homes, but the protesters said they do not trust its promises.
